title: The stable after 0.38.231: lights you tap in the 3D house, power teams, a phone's room scan as a floor plan, steadier rooms, and safer saves
body_markdown:
### New
- **This is everything since 0.38.231 in one go,** written as how it works now. The betas' notes under it are the steps along the way; where they differ, this one is right.
- **Lights in the 3D house.** Tap a light in Live Aboard to switch it. Lights show as buttons under where they hang, can be moved in the 3D editor, string lights are drawn, and a room can work as one light switch. Unlocking a lock from the map asks first, white-only bulbs get a warmth slider, and a light's card has a Details link to Home Assistant's own window for it.
- **Power teams.** Smart bulbs on a wall dimmer, or lights that always have power, act as one light that follows the day. Lights found on after a restart are put right.
- **No floor plan? Ways to get one.** Start a blank floor, use a drawing you have, or upload a phone's room scan: its rooms, doors, windows and furniture come with it, and it finds its own place. When a plan is moved, what was placed on it can move with it, and lining up plans can suggest a fit.
- **Let Claude draw your rooms (experimental).** With an AI Task set up, Claude reads a plan and proposes room outlines that you check and keep.
- **Live Aboard** opens on the whole house with labels that follow the zoom, glass walls, a look for each screen, room chips and a room panel, kitchen and bathroom furniture, one-tap room sets, people and cars, covered patios, open decks and an Outside floor, and a ready-made Christmas tree.
- **Keys can keep their room (an option, off unless you turn it on).** Settings → Presence → Home/Away Timeout: things no person carries can stay in their last room for hours. Every device's area sensor and tracker also gain `last_room`, the room it was last seen in.

### Changed
- **Home Assistant 2024.8 or newer.** It said 2024.1, but before 2024.8 the sensors of the devices PadSpan tracks could not be added. Every release from 2024.8 to 2026.11 is now tested on each change.
- **Rooms are steadier.** A device that goes quiet keeps its room instead of drifting to another, possibly on another floor; a device nobody heard no longer "arrives"; a pinned beacon reports its room once; and a room change is never sent twice running. On a real house's four-hour recording, wrong room changes for devices that never moved halved compared with 0.38.231, and repeated room-change events went from 882 to 3.
- **Room tracking never waits.** It stalled for half a minute or more each time a calibration point was added, while a model only the "Learned model" setting uses was retrained; that model now trains in the background, and only when that setting is on. The health pages and the device list next to a busy street are much faster.
- **Lighter Home Assistant database.** Signal readings and other per-poll values are no longer written to Home Assistant's history; rooms, home or away and names still are.
- **A new install starts with Enhanced security on.** A home already set up keeps the switch as it has it.
- **Receivers' agreement in System Critics now means what it says**, and it no longer changes room decisions.

### Fixed
- **Saves are checked.** A save of PadSpan's main files that does not reach the disk is reported in Settings → Repairs instead of passing silently, and the next good save takes the notice down.
- **A saved file PadSpan cannot read is kept,** renamed beside the others and named once in the log, instead of being written over.
- **Junk is refused in words:** a command with something missing, "nan" or "inf", numbers or texts too large to keep, and lists of the wrong kind. A settings save that is refused changes nothing at all.
- **Hidden devices stay hidden, and named devices stay listed** however long they are silent.
- **PadSpan does not fetch from your own machine:** a robot vacuum's or the ESPresense Companion's address must be a device on your network.
- **In the panel,** Escape closes every card and sheet, dialogs keep the keyboard and give it back, and wide tables on a phone scroll inside their own box.

title: One write per automatic calibration point; Calibration accuracy worked out in the background; Device list builds faster next to a street; Dialogs keep the keyboard; Escape closes every card and sheet; A robot vacuum's or ESPresense Companion's address must be on your network; Settings with a few choices refuse any other; Health checks answer faster; The panel's files are registered once; Wide tables scroll on their own on a phone; Radio QA's propagation card no longer says "Loading" for good; Radio Reset clears a receiver's signal readings; Room changes no longer wait for the learned model; Sample mode's calibration check shows the sample house's points; Limits on names, notes, positions and lists; A tier override and a Pro feature in one save; Three more saved files are set aside, not written over
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **A pinned beacon's automatic calibration points write the calibration file once each, not twice.** Each point was saved, and then trimming the beacon's oldest point (50 are kept) saved the whole file again: about 1,400 writes a day of a several-megabyte file in a busy house, wearing an SD card for nothing. The trim now goes in the same save; the points kept are the same.
- **Opening Health or the calibration model no longer freezes Home Assistant while the accuracy is worked out.** The calibration accuracy compares every calibration point with every other; with a few hundred points that takes seconds, and Home Assistant could do nothing else meanwhile (no automations, no other integrations, a frozen dashboard). It is now worked out in the background, as Home Assistant does with its own slow jobs.
- **Building the device list no longer slows down with the square of the passing crowd.** When many passing devices are taken for one rotating device (all those that say nothing and are heard by the same receivers, or send the same kind of Apple message), each one merged in re-read and re-sorted the whole list of addresses gathered so far. Hundreds of them took a large share of every build, and Home Assistant waits while the list is built. They are now gathered once per group; the list is the same.
- **A dialog keeps the keyboard while it is open.** The panel's dialogs (a device's or a room's details, Rename, the release notes, Point Align) and the Atlas's cards and sheets did not take the keyboard: Tab went on through the page behind them, and on closing the focus fell back to the top of the page. They now take it when they open, Tab stays inside them, and when they close the focus goes back to what you pressed to open them.
- **The focus stays put when a view refreshes.** A view drawn again every few seconds replaced the button or field that had the focus, so the keyboard lost its place. The focus now goes to the same control in the new drawing.
- **Escape closes the phone menu, the Atlas builder's guide and the Atlas's cards.** On the phone menu, the Atlas builder's guide, the room, door, light and activity cards on the flat Atlas and the wall screen, the emergency lights card and the people, tag and receiver cards on the map, Escape did nothing; only ✕ or a tap outside closed them. Escape now does what ✕ does. Where Escape already meant something else (a field you are typing in, the 3D view's own keys), it still does.
- **The robot vacuum import and the ESPresense Companion import fetch only from your home network.** Both read from the address you type. They also took an address that is this Home Assistant machine itself (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) or a link-local one (`169.254.x.x`, where a cloud server answers questions about itself), followed a redirect to any address, and an address with a `?` in it lost the path PadSpan adds, so they fetched the wrong page. Now an address that is, or whose name leads to, this machine, a link-local, multicast or empty address is refused in words before anything is fetched, a redirect is not followed, and a `?` or `#` in the address no longer replaces the path. Addresses on your home network (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, 172.16 to 172.31, fd00::) and names that lead to them work as before. If you saved the Companion's address as `localhost`, use its address on your network instead (for example `http://192.168.1.50:8267`).
- **A setting with a few fixed choices refuses a word it does not know.** The data mode (Live or Sample), the positioning method (matched to calibration points, or the learned model), the tier override for looking at a lower tier, and the automatic offset mode took any word, sent by a script or an automation calling PadSpan directly, and stored a fallback without saying so: an unknown data mode switched your house to the sample house, an unknown positioning method went back to calibration matching, and an unknown tier cleared the override. Now such a word is refused in words and the setting stays as it was. The panel sends only the known choices, so nothing changes on screen. The panel style still falls back to Classic for a word it does not know, so a bad value can never leave the panel on a style that does not load.
- **The Health and Q&A checks no longer hold up Home Assistant for seconds.** Layout checks, the propagation grade and the system critics each worked out the calibration accuracy from scratch, comparing every calibration point with every other, and Home Assistant waited while they did: over a second each with a few hundred points, every 30 seconds while the page was open. That work is now about half as long, and done once until a calibration point changes.
- **No "register_static_path is deprecated" line in Home Assistant's log.** On Home Assistant 2024.8 to 2025.7, each time PadSpan reloaded, Home Assistant logged that PadSpan used an old way to serve the panel's files and asked for a bug report. PadSpan registered the same files again on every reload, and the second time fell back to the old call. The files are now registered once each time Home Assistant starts.
- **On a phone, a wide table scrolls sideways by itself.** Overview's All objects, View radios list and Rooms lists are wider than a phone, so the whole sheet slid sideways under your finger, its title and filters with it. The table now scrolls sideways inside its own box and the sheet stays put.
- **Radio QA's propagation card says when there is nothing to show.** In Sample mode, or when the analysis could not be loaded, the card said "Loading propagation analysis..." and never changed. It now says there is no analysis for this house yet, or that it could not be loaded.
- **Resetting a receiver no longer leaves its signal readings behind.** Radio Reset forgot what the receiver had heard but kept its recent signal readings of each device, and a device only that receiver had heard kept them for as long as Home Assistant ran. They now go with the rest.
- **Room changes and alerts were late by up to a minute every few minutes in homes with pinned beacons.** A pinned beacon adds a calibration point by itself about every ten minutes, and each time PadSpan stopped tracking until it had trained the learned model (Random Forest) again: about 25 seconds on a desktop computer, longer on a Raspberry Pi, while Home Assistant itself also ran slower. Only the "Learned model" positioning setting uses that model; the default, "Matched to calibration points", never did. Now tracking never waits for it. With the default setting the model is not trained at all, and the Health page says "not used" for it instead of showing it as a problem. With "Learned model" chosen it trains in the background, and PadSpan matches calibration points until it is ready.
- **Settings → Tracking → Check Now works in Sample mode.** It said "undefined calibration points · newest is unknown age old". It now shows the sample house's calibration points, how old they are, and its receivers.
- **PadSpan no longer keeps text, numbers or lists no home would have.** Sent by a script or an automation calling PadSpan directly (the panel never sends them), PadSpan stored as it came: a name or label of 100,000 characters or with an invisible NUL character in it, a receiver or beacon at a position of 1e308 metres, a list of 10,000 followed devices or hidden plans, and settings nested 200 levels deep. Every save, backup and screen then carried them. These are now refused in words, before anything changes. The limits are far past anything a home uses: a name, label, room or id up to 200 characters, a note up to 2,000, a position within 10 km of the house's origin, up to 500 rooms and 1,000 pins on a plan in one save, up to 5,000 entries in a setting's list, and up to 10 levels in a record sent whole.
- **A wall keeps only what a wall is.** A wall saved from the panel or a script kept every field it was sent, whatever its name. Now it keeps its name, points, floor, material, how much it weakens a signal, its railing, its door or window sensor, opener and lock, and whether that sensor reads backwards. A wall's name is up to 200 characters and a wall up to 1,000 points.
- **A Pro feature saved together with a tier override follows that override.** The tier override (Settings, development view: "Look at this install as tier") lets a PadSpan Pro install look at what a free or Bright install sees. A single save that set the override and a Pro-only setting (Forensics recording, or who "you" are for Locate) judged the Pro setting by the tier from before the save, so the same save sent twice gave two results: lowering the tier and turning Forensics on in one save turned it on, and the next identical save turned it off. The Pro setting is now judged by the tier the save leaves, so it stays off at a lowered tier and works at once when the override is lifted. An override still never raises the tier past your licence.
- **The object history and the opt-in report's two files are kept when PadSpan cannot read them.** Since the last release a PadSpan file in `.storage` that holds the wrong kind of data is renamed to `<name>.unreadable.<date>` and named once in Home Assistant's log, instead of being started empty and written over. Three files still missed that: the object history (`padspan_ha.object_history`, the devices PadSpan remembers after they go quiet), and the opt-in report's run log and usage counts (`padspan_ha.perf_runs`, `padspan_ha.telemetry_counters`). They are now set aside and named the same way.

title: Home Assistant 2024.8 or newer; "nan" and "inf" are not numbers; A number too large to save is refused; A plan's picture, pins and placement are checked before they are saved; Very long tester sign-up text answers at once; Keys can keep their room; A saved file PadSpan cannot read is kept, not replaced; Saves are checked against the disk; A value of the wrong kind is refused, not a failure
body_markdown:
### New
- **`last_room` on the area sensor and the device tracker:** the room the device was last seen in. It stays there after the device reads not_home, so an automation or a card can still say where it was left.
- **An option: keys, tags and other things can stay in their room for hours.** It is off unless you turn it on, and nothing changes until you do. Every device switches to not_home once it has not been heard for the away timeout (5 minutes unless you changed it), so keys in a drawer or a tag on a bag go "away" while they sit in the kitchen. If you would rather they stayed in their room, set a number of hours in Settings → Presence → Home/Away Timeout, under "Things keep their room": 0.5 to 48 hours, or 0 for off. What a person carries still goes away after the away timeout; anything nobody carries keeps the room it was last seen in for the hours you set, then switches to not_home. This is the area sensor and the device tracker in Home Assistant; the PadSpan panel, arrive and leave alerts and events are unchanged.
- **Before you turn it on: what counts as carried.** A device is carried when it is added to a person in Home Assistant (Settings → People → Track devices), is picked for them in Live Aboard (Furnish → People & devices), or has the person's name. Every other named device counts as a thing. A phone or watch that is not linked to a person would read as home in its last room for those hours after it has left, so add each one to its person first. A car's tag does the same: it stays in the garage for those hours after the car has gone.

### Changed
- **PadSpan needs Home Assistant 2024.8 or newer.** It said 2024.1, but on Home Assistant before 2024.8 the sensors of the devices it tracks could not be added, so a device had no room sensor. HACS now offers PadSpan only on 2024.8 and newer. If your Home Assistant is older, update Home Assistant first. PadSpan has been checked on Home Assistant releases from 2024.8 to 2026.11.
- **Less work after each save.** After a save, PadSpan used to read the whole file back and unpack it. With a large calibration file, which is saved about once a minute while beacons calibrate themselves, that held Home Assistant up for a moment each time. The check below reads the file without unpacking it.

### Fixed
- **"nan" and "inf" are refused where a number is expected.** A light's size and turn, a receiver's height and its signal offset, and the end of a guest's stay took the words "nan" and "inf" as numbers and stored them, where they spoil every position worked out from them and are saved as nothing at all. They are refused now, with the rest of what is not a number. A guest's stay changed later can no longer end further ahead than one started now can (a year).
- **A number too large to be saved no longer stops PadSpan saving.** A few places took a whole number of any size: the headcount you train the occupancy estimate with, a storey's level in Floor Heights, and the setup helper's snooze count. Sent a number larger than Home Assistant can write (by a script or an automation calling PadSpan directly; the panel never sends one), PadSpan kept it, and from then on every save of its settings or of the house model failed until Home Assistant restarted, losing every change made meanwhile. The headcount is now a whole number from 0 to 1,000, a level is between -1,000 and 1,000, and a capture's page offset can no longer ask for a page past the end of any capture.
- **A plan's picture is checked before it is replaced.** Replace Image took anything at all: a payload that was not a picture was written over the plan's picture as it came, and one that was not even base64 failed with "Unknown error". It now takes a PNG, at most 20 MB, as an upload does, and refuses anything else before touching the plan. A crop or a turn that is not numbers is refused before the picture is written, not after.
- **A plan's pins can no longer be wiped by a bad save.** A save of a plan's beacons that held anything but beacons removed every beacon from the plan and then failed; a receiver pin at a position that was not a number, or a plan level of null, failed with "Unknown error". The pins must be a list of pins now, a position that is not a number is the corner as a missing one always was, and a level that is not a number is the ground floor.
- **A plan's placement keeps only what a placement holds.** The Measure tool's save stored every field it was sent, whatever its name, as part of where the plan sits; one with no measurements in it failed afterwards. Only the placement's own fields are kept now, each of its own kind.
- **A tester sign-up with very long text no longer holds up Home Assistant.** The check that keeps keys and tokens out of a sign-up took time that grew with the square of the text's length: 100,000 characters sent straight to Home Assistant (the panel stops at 500) held all of Home Assistant for about a minute. It now reads at most the first 1,000 characters of each box, more than any box takes; the answer is the same.
- **A PadSpan file that holds the wrong kind of data is set aside, not written over.** When one of PadSpan's saved files in Home Assistant's `.storage` folder held something PadSpan could not use (after a hand edit, or a file written by a version that kept it differently), PadSpan started that part empty without saying so, and the next save replaced the file. For the settings, floor plans, rooms and devices that happened as Home Assistant started. Now the file is renamed to `<name>.unreadable.<date>` beside the others, one error in Home Assistant's log names it, and PadSpan starts that part empty, as Home Assistant itself does with a file it cannot open. Restore a backup, or put the file back once a version that reads it is running.
- **The same for a file that is not a Home Assistant storage file at all**, for example one cut down to `[]` by hand. It filled the log with the same error each time PadSpan read it, and two parts of PadSpan stopped loading at start-up without saying why. It is now set aside and named once, like a file of the wrong kind. A file that cannot be read at all (a disk error) is still left exactly where it is.
- **A save that did not reach the disk is no longer called saved.** After saving its rooms, maps, settings, calibration or Live Aboard file, PadSpan read the file back but only checked that something was there. When Home Assistant could not write the file (a full or read-only disk), the old file was still there, so the save passed. PadSpan now checks that the file holds exactly what Home Assistant wrote. A save that did not land is written to the log and shown as a notice under Settings, Repairs; the notice goes away by itself when a save works again. The check only reads: it never changes, deletes or puts back a file.
- **A value of the wrong kind no longer ends in "Unknown error".** Sent a number where a list of points belongs, or the like, by a script or an automation calling PadSpan directly (the panel never sends one), a signal wall, an open edge, a WLED team, a room outline and a device's "How we know" answered with Home Assistant's "Unknown error" and an error in its log, and a calibration point with Python's own words. A wall, a team and a calibration point are now refused in words and change nothing; an outline or a device detail of the wrong kind is left out of the answer.

title: A command with something missing says what; Quiet devices keep their room, arrivals need a device to be heard; A refused settings save changes nothing; Hidden devices stay hidden, labelled devices stay listed, and the device list keeps its order
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **An action that failed with "Unknown error" now says what is missing.** 22 of PadSpan's commands answered a message that left out something they need (a plan, a device, a height, a width) with an error and no reason: merging or renaming a device, a receiver's height, placing a light, beacon or receiver, a blank floor, Suggest a fit, a plan's scale, a headcount and others. Home Assistant now refuses such a message itself and names what is missing. The panel sends all of these, so nothing changes on screen; a script or tool that calls PadSpan's commands gets the clear answer.
- **A device that has gone quiet stays in the room it was in.** A device that left the house, or was switched off, could be shown moving to another room about half a minute later, sometimes on another floor, with a room-change alert to match. Nothing had heard it move: the receivers that heard it best had let go of their readings, and an old reading from a receiver that seldom heard it was all that was left. With nothing new from any receiver for about 15 seconds (three polls at the default 5 s), a device now keeps its room until it is heard again.
- **No "arrived" for a device nobody heard.** When PadSpan stopped listing a device that had been silent for a long time (at the BLE Advertisement Timeout, or when its history ran out), it was counted as arriving: the arrive alert, `padspan_device_arrived` and arrive rules ran hours or days after it had left, and its device tracker read its old room for two minutes instead of `not_home`. An arrival now needs the device to be heard. A device that drops off the list while it still counts as home is now reported as departed when it is dropped; before, it never was.
- **A pinned beacon reports its room once.** A pinned beacon is shown in its pin's room. When its solved position fell in the room next door, it sent a room-change alert, a movement-history entry and a tag event again and again while the room it was shown in never changed. It now reports a room change only when the room it is shown in changes.
- **A room-change event or alert is not sent twice running.** `padspan_room_change` events (and the tag scans with them) and Follow's room alerts are spaced at least 30 and 60 seconds apart. A device that changed room, went back within that time and changed again was reported as making the same change twice, with nothing between; and after PadSpan had lost sight of a device for a minute, its next event could start in a room the last event had not ended in. Each event and alert now starts in the room the last one ended in, and a device back in the room last reported sends nothing. A device not listed for a minute or two and then heard in another room is reported as moving from the room it was shown in, where it was reported as placed from nowhere.
- **Receivers are no longer marked unreliable for hearing devices in other rooms.** A receiver was marked wrong each time it heard a device that was in another room, which is most of what any receiver hears. In a house with devices in several rooms every receiver drifted to about 50% reliability: System Critics listed them as "disagrees with consensus", and their readings were weakened by up to 5 dB whenever a room was picked by strongest signal. A receiver is now judged only on the devices it hears loudest, so the figure in System Critics means what it says. The figure is also no longer used to weaken a receiver's readings: it is worked out from PadSpan's own room answers, so used that way it marked down receivers that were right when the answer was wrong, and in testing it did not put more devices in the right room.
- **A settings save that is refused changes nothing.** When one save carried several settings and one of them was refused, PadSpan had sometimes already acted on another: a newly followed device was given a name, an unfollowed one was cleared from the map, the usage report's counts were started again, or a use was counted. Everything in a save is now checked first, and a refused save does nothing at all.
- **"Not a number" is no longer saved as a number.** A value such as `nan` or `inf` sent for a numeric setting (the room change delay, the away timeout, the signal settings, the home's latitude and longitude, the zoom and others) was saved as that setting's highest allowed value. It is now refused with an error, for every numeric setting, and nothing is saved.
- **Two settings no longer fail without an answer.** The list of extra tabs and the receivers' signal adjustments, sent with something that was not a tab name or not a number, made the save fail with no error. They now answer with an error and save nothing.
- **Lists of maps, lights and devices hold names only.** Blank entries, and entries that were not text (they were saved as the words "None" or "[1]"), are no longer kept in the hidden maps, hidden lights, followed devices, beacon tuning and grouping, stationary references and the ESPresense room names.
- **The ESPresense Companion address must be a web address.** It is saved only when it starts with `http://` or `https://`, or is empty to clear it. Anything else is refused, and the address already saved stays.
- **A number that cannot be saved is refused wherever it sits.** A number that is not finite, or a whole number too large for the settings file, inside a list or a group of values (a saved look, a rule, a door group) was kept as it came. Such a save is now refused whole, and nothing is saved.
- **A device hidden by an ingest rule is really left out of the device list.** A rule on a plain device's address, or on its maker's prefix (the `ingest_rules` setting), counted the device as hidden and listed it all the same; only iBeacons and phones with a key were kept out. A hidden device is now left out however it would have been listed: as a plain Bluetooth device, as the Home Assistant entity that tracks it, or from the object history. While it is hidden its place in the object history is kept the way a device that is not being heard is kept: for good if it has a label, and for the object history time (one day unless you changed it) if it has none. Take the rule away and a labelled device is back as it was, first-seen date and all; one without a label that was hidden for longer than that comes back as a new device. The count of hidden devices in the snapshot's summary counts each one once.
- **`excluded_objects` hides a device by its address too.** An entry hid a device only when it was an iBeacon's or a phone's key; a plain device's address hid nothing. An entry can now be written any way the device list shows a device: its address (capitals or small letters), its key (`ble:…`, `ibeacon:…`, `irk:…`, `entity:…`), or, for one beacon of a pack that shares an id, the id followed by that beacon's address.
- **A labelled device that goes quiet stays in the device list.** A plain Bluetooth device you had named, not heard for longer than the object history time, was dropped from the list and came back as a new device the next time it was heard: its name was kept, but the list looked for it under the wrong id and took the device for one nobody had named. It now stays listed, with the date it was first seen. The same goes for a device whose name is held only in PadSpan's device registry.
- **Devices heard at the same moment keep the same order after a restart.** Adverts of exactly the same age came out in an order that changed each time Home Assistant started, and the device list was built in that order. They now go by address.

title: Tidier floor controls, room list and page titles; Lists and tables that fit a phone, and ages you can read; Live Tracker, Bluetooth and Traceback tidied up, on a phone and on a wide screen; The panel's frame tidied: phone bars, loading, tab strips; Errors PadSpan handles quietly are counted; Enhanced security starts on for a new install; A safety backup before calibration points are cleared; Links drawn as text work from the keyboard; Housekeeping: more checks before a release
body_markdown:
### New
- **Diagnostics lists the errors PadSpan handled quietly.** When one part of PadSpan fails, the rest carries on, and until now nothing said so. Each such place in the code now counts how often it happens and keeps the last error, in memory only, since Home Assistant started. An administrator sees them in Diagnostics (QA → Go to Diagnostics) under "Errors PadSpan handled quietly": where, how many times, the last error and when. The list is not part of the report you send to support, and nothing is written to the log or to disk.

### Changed
- **The opt-in usage report carries those counts.** For up to 20 of those places it sends the place's fixed name from the code and a number, so the ones that really happen in people's houses can be found and fixed. It never sends an error's text. The README's list of what the report sends says so.
- **A new install starts with Enhanced security on.** From its first day, changes to the home's shared setup (clearing calibration, deleting rooms or devices, resets, and the rest of the list under Who can change what) need a Home Assistant administrator, while everyone in the house can still view and use PadSpan. A home that is already set up keeps the switch exactly as it has it; it is under Settings → Tracking → Enhanced security.
- **Clearing calibration points takes a safety backup first.** Clear All (Calibration) and a map's Clear (Settings) now take the automatic backup before any point is removed, so the points can be brought back from Manage → Backup & Restore. If the backup can't be made, nothing is removed and the reply says so.
- **A phone's key stays with administrators.** Settings sent to someone who is not an administrator carry each saved phone's name and no key. Testing a key and looking for keys are for administrators, as saving and removing one already were.
- **Traceback and movement history have a largest request.** One request returns at most 4,000 Traceback frames or 200 movement-history entries, which is the most the panel asks for.
- **The integration's icon and logo are served as two single files**, at the addresses they always had.
- **The README's privacy section now covers the shared furniture library and the AI reads**: what each sends, and when.
- **A refused clear says why.** When clearing calibration points is refused (the safety backup could not be made), the message shows the reason; it used to read "[object Object]".
- **More mistakes are caught before a release reaches you.** Every release now checks the Python for names that are used but never defined (the kind of slip that made "Suggest a fit" always say there was no fit in 0.38.256), and checks the panel's code against 42 more rules for plain mistakes. Three small slips these turned up are fixed; none of them changed what you see.
- **Each of the panel's files loads once, and fresh after an update.** A few helper files were loaded without the stamp that tells your browser a new version is out, and with the PadSpan page and the Atlas page open in the same browser many files were downloaded and run twice. Every file now has one address.
- **The download zip is no longer stored in the repository.** Each release still builds it and attaches it to the GitHub release, which is where HACS gets it.

### Fixed
- **The floor controls above the Overview and Traceback maps wrap in whole pieces on a phone.** A label ("Gap:", "Spacing:", "L/R:") used to end one line while its slider started the next. Each label now stays with its own slider and value. On Traceback, Save and Reset no longer touch each other or the number before them. Nothing was renamed or moved, and the row on a wide screen is as it was.
- **Settings, on a phone: the room's colour dot stays beside its name.** The dot used to jump above the name, and a name as short as "Bathroom" was broken in the middle of the word, because the name had only a narrow strip of the row. The name now has more of the row on a phone, and when it does run to a second line the dot stays beside the first.
- **Presence: a scanner's name is no longer cut short while there is room in its card.** In a narrow card the two counts ("tagged", "untagged") move to the line below the name instead of squeezing it down to a few letters. A device's name and its RSSI now run on as one line of text, so a device takes two lines where it took three, and the RSSI is no longer cut off beside a long name.
- **Monitor, Health and Forensics: the page title sits where it does on the other pages.** There was about 40 px more empty space round these three titles.
- **Occupancy on a phone: room names are whole again.** In "Rooms with evidence" the room's name was squeezed into a sliver and broke letter by letter. On a narrow screen each room's name now has a line of its own, with its people, phones, sensors and agreement under it. On a desktop the table is as it was.
- **Manage on a phone: the Delete button of every area is on the screen.** The areas table was wider than the screen. A long area ID now wraps onto a second line instead of pushing Delete off the edge.
- **Manage: area IDs are readable.** They were tiny dark grey text on a near-black card; they are now the same size and grey as the other IDs on that page.
- **Manage: the cards on the Data tab no longer touch,** and the help button sits beside the Danger Zone heading instead of alone on a line under it.
- **Devices: "last heard" reads as time, not a count of seconds.** A device heard 56 days ago said "4837956s ago"; it now says "56 days ago" (or seconds, minutes or hours for something more recent).
- **Devices: Details, Rename and Untag stay side by side.** When a row ran out of room the three buttons broke apart differently on every row. They now move to the next line together, on a phone as well.
- **Buttons that looked like text boxes are button sized.** "Find" on Presence, "Search window" on Forensics, "Save & Refresh" and "Save" on Occupancy, and the list buttons under Rooms, Objects and Bluetooth radios on the Overview stretched across their whole card.
- **Live Tracker: the search box no longer sits on the scanner strip.** The counter (rooms, tracked, radios), the search box and the scanner strip over the map could land on top of each other: on a 1280-wide screen the search hid the first scanner codes, and on a phone it hid the counter as well. They now share one row that never overlaps. With room, each is where it was. With less, the search moves over; on a phone the counter and the search share the first line and the scanner strip takes the second.
- **Bluetooth, "Who hears what": text you can read at any width.** The graph's text grew and shrank with the window: about 4 px on a phone, about 19 px on a wide monitor. It is now the same size as the rest of the page everywhere. Names are no longer cut at 38 letters with free space beside them: a name is shortened only when the graph is too narrow to show it, as on a phone.
- **Bluetooth, "Who hears what": device names no longer drawn over each other.** Where two scanners sat close together, their devices could land on the same line.
- **Bluetooth on a phone: the tabs line up with the cards.** The tab strip was a few pixels wider than the cards above it and its two rows were uneven. It now ends where the cards end, three equal tabs over two equal ones. The Search and Source labels sit on one line.
- **Traceback: the legend under the map names the floors.** It listed the file name of every floor plan, joined with "+", and ran off the right edge ("4 Posi"). It now shows each floor's name (Lower, Main, Upper) and stays inside the map. A level whose plans belong to no named floor still shows the plans' names, shortened to fit.
- **Traceback: a tag no longer covers the name of the room it is in.** A tag's marker and its room chip ("Garage") sat right on the room's own name ("Garage"). The marker now stands just above the name (or just below it), on Playback and on New Objects.
- **Traceback on a phone: tidy tabs, and "Filter:" in one piece.** Playback, New Objects, Insights and Busy Times each stay on one line and share a row, with Full house activity on the next, instead of labels wrapped over two and three lines at different heights. Under Distance Traveled, "Filter:" no longer breaks into "Filte" and "r:".
- **The phone's top bar and bottom tab bar match the page.** With the 2025 panel style (Settings → Appearance → Panel Style) both bars were brown against a green-black page, as if they belonged to another app. They now have the same colour as the sidebar. The Classic style is unchanged.
- **The panel opens in the style you chose.** The 2025 style used to go on only once the settings had loaded, so for the first seconds you saw the Classic menu and colours and then everything jumped. Each browser now remembers the style and uses it from the start. The first time a browser opens the panel it still starts in Classic until the settings arrive.
- **Health says "loading" until it has something to show.** Opened directly, it showed "Rooms: 0", "Radios: 0" and "Refresh: —ms" as if they were readings. Those lines now say "loading…" until the first answer arrives, and the Scan and Status badges at the top show "…" instead of a dash.
- **Health counts your devices.** "Tags/Objects" read 0 in a house with thousands of devices, because it counted only Home Assistant's own room-tracker entities. It now counts every device PadSpan hears, the same ones the Devices page lists.
- **Atlas no longer says the same thing twice.** While the yellow first-time tip is showing, the line of small print beside the title is hidden. Press "Got it" and the line is back as before.
- **Mapping reads "1 map" or "9 maps"**, not "9 map(s)", and a plan's "updated" time is shown as a date and time in your own time zone instead of a raw timestamp.
- **Mapping's tabs show that there are more.** On a phone the row of tabs was cut off mid-word at the edge of the screen. The edge now fades where more tabs lie beyond it, on either side, so it is clear the row slides.
- **Calibration and Manage tabs on a phone.** When the tabs wrap to a second row, each row now has its own line under it, so the highlighted tab sits on a line instead of floating. On Calibration's Results, "Guided calibration" now sits under the heading on the left when it does not fit beside it.
- **Links drawn as text work from the keyboard.** A name that opens a device or a receiver, a room in a list, "Hide these tips", "Skip setup", "Open Setup", "Go →", "+ Add Identity", the count badges that filter Devices, and "Cancel" while placing a receiver or a beacon: Tab now reaches each one, Enter or Space does what a click does, and a screen reader says it is a button. They look the same as before.
- **A long session on a map no longer builds up work for the browser.** Mapping → Edit, Mapping → Rooms and Calibration's maps left listeners behind on every redraw (five for each receiver marker in Edit), and every mouse move ran all of them. They are removed now; dragging a receiver and panning a map work as before.
- **A name with a quote or an apostrophe in it stays a name.** Where a name is written into the page's markup, both kinds of quote are escaped as well as the angle brackets and the ampersand. Radio QA's receiver names and the Bluetooth view's raw data show an ampersand or an angle bracket as written.

title: A ready-made Christmas tree in Build
body_markdown:
### New
- **Build has a ready-made Christmas tree.** In Live Aboard's Furnish, Build now lists "Christmas tree" after Plant: a 2 m fir with no pot, placed with one tap like the other ready-made pieces.

title: A fir for the plant, so a Christmas tree looks like one
body_markdown:
### New
- **A plant can be a fir.** In Live Aboard's Build, Plant now offers "fir" beside bush, tree, palm and cactus: tiers of green that narrow to a point, on a short trunk, with or without a pot. It is the shape for a Christmas tree; a bush stretched to that height ended in a dark dome. A plant already in your house is unchanged.

title: A wall that arranges its own floors covers no room; A wall stacks its floors as saved again
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **A wall draws its floors one on top of the other, with the saved Spacing and L/R, as before.** For about an hour a wall arranged its floors for its own screen and stepped them sideways. That made the house larger and broke what a stack is for: reading the floors as one building. The stack is back as every wall's default. The arrangement stays for a wall whose link carries `?arrange=1`.
- **The wall still measures how large the house is drawn** against what its screen allows, but it only moves in by itself on an arrangement it made, never on a saved stack.

### Fixed
- **On a wall whose link carries `?arrange=1`, no room sits under the floor above.** The arrangement allowed 2% of the whole house under a higher floor's plate, which on a real house was a third of one deck. No single room may now lose more than a sliver.

title: A wall draws the house as large as its screen allows
body_markdown:
### New
- **A wall checks, after every drawing, that the house is as large as the screen allows.** If it ever opens far back (under 85% of that size), it moves in on the house by itself, and with the usage report on it says so once a page (`wall_fill:ok`, `low` or `closer`). `tools/wall_fill_check.py` runs the same check on the demo house or a real Home Assistant at any screen size.

### Changed
- **A wall screen arranges the floors for its own shape, so the house fills the screen.** The flat Atlas on a wall (`?kiosk=1`) used the Spacing and L/R saved under Layout & view, one pair of numbers for every screen and for the Overview tab's map too. A spacing that suits a narrow map stacks the floors into a tall, thin tower on a wide wall, which then shrinks to fit its height: a small house with space either side. A wall now works out the arrangement itself each time it draws: on a wide screen the floors step sideways, on a tall one they stay a stack, and every room stays in sight. On a three-floor house on a 1080p wall that is about 40% larger than the saved spacing gave. The saved Spacing and L/R still set every other screen; moving either slider on the wall itself takes over there until Reset view.
- **A wall has no scroll bars.** Zoomed in, the map is dragged or pinched as before.

### Fixed
- **Floors set far apart sideways draw properly.** A floor's plate is 18 units thick straight down (its sides used to slide sideways with the L/R spacing), and each floor's number badge stays at its own floor's corner (past the old 760-unit canvas they were pulled into a column over other floors' rooms).

title: The launch-price card for a year's key
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **The "launch price ends November 30" card now also shows to anyone with PadSpan Pro or Bright Pro for a year**, once, until the end of November 30, with one more line: pay with the email your key was sent to and that key becomes Pro for life. A key that is already for life never sees it.

title: The usage report: its one question reaches every opt-in, and three things it could not say
body_markdown:
### New
- **The usage report says which store keeps PadSpan up to date, and whether your automations use it.** Two new lines in the opt-in report: `store`, one word for Home Assistant's Marketplace, HACS, or neither when PadSpan was copied in by hand; and `used_in`, how many automations and how many scripts use one of PadSpan's entities or devices. Two counts, never which ones. The Preview shows both, and the README's list of what the report sends has them.
- **Deleting PadSpan with the report on sends one last report that says so.** It carries the anonymous ID, the day, the version and that one flag, and nothing about the house, so a removed install can be told from a machine that is switched off. With the report off, nothing is sent.

### Changed
- **The optional question, where you heard about PadSpan, now reaches every way of opting in.** It was asked only after a yes on the opt-in card. It is now asked once per install whichever way the report comes on (the card, Settings, the tick box on the free trial) and when a free trial, a tester sign-up or a free year starts: a card on the Overview with one-tap answers and Skip. An answer or Skip ends it for good, it is never shown on a wall screen, and a house whose report was already on is still not asked: the choice stays under Settings → Tracking → Help improve PadSpan.

title: Room sets: odd-shaped rooms, doorways and kitchen corners; The launch price ends November 30; The usage report counts irk-capture keys apart; Live Aboard: Rooms ▾ by default; Usage report: Live Aboard's Look and rooms, and Furnish's room sets; WLED outputs: a made-up example address
body_markdown:
### New
- **One card on Overview: "The launch price ends November 30".** It says that PadSpan Pro for life is $89 CAD, once, until November 30 (then $168), with a button to buy at padspan.traks.ca. Only an administrator sees it, only on a house without a running paid licence (no key, a trial, or a licence that has run out), and only once: it is not shown again after a reload, and No thanks hides it for good. It is never shown on a wall screen, and it goes by itself at the end of November 30 (Pacific time). Nothing about it is sent in the usage report.

### Changed
- **The opt-in usage report now tells keys from an irk-capture ESP32 apart.** A key saved from an irk-capture ESP32 (in the phone wizard, or found by Auto-detect in the IRK Manager) is counted as one, with whether it works, and the report says how many irk-capture ESP32s Home Assistant has: counts only, never names, and only while the report is on.
- **Live Aboard shows one Rooms ▾ button at the top on every screen**, not a row of every room's name. It lists every named room under its floor's name, as before; pick one to go there. If you liked the row, tick **Room chips along the top** in ⋯ (on a wide screen; phones and wall screens always have Rooms ▾). Like the other ticks there, it is kept for that screen only.
- **The WLED card's network output hint shows a made-up example address (192.168.0.119).** It shows when a network output's address is missing or incomplete; before, its example was an address from a real network.

### Fixed
- **Room sets use the room's other walls before leaving a piece out.** In an L-shaped room a set could keep the bed and lose the wardrobe and the dresser. A piece with no room on the wall it was meant for now goes on another wall of the room. It still never overlaps anything, blocks a door or runs past a corner.
- **Room sets keep out of doorways.** A cabinet or a desk could stick partly into an opening with no door in it. Now nothing from a set stands in the way through a door or a doorway, on either side.
- **An L-shaped kitchen closes its corner.** When the walls didn't divide evenly, a gap was left where the two runs meet. Now the run is closed up to the corner with a unit sized to what is left (or the end unit made a little wider), and the worktop and wall cabinets run round the corner. The run along the side wall now starts right in the corner.
- **The bathroom set puts the basin under a window**, as the kitchen sets put the sink, when the toilet and basin already pass under one. Nothing is left out for it.
- **Hang on wall measures a sink or a basin to its worktop or rim.** It used to be measured to the top of its tap, so a sink hung under a low window went to another wall. Now it hangs under the window, with its tap in front of the glass, as when you drag it there.

### Usage report (opt-in)
- Counts of a Look picked in Live Aboard's Views ▾ (only its kind: Classic, Studio, a Showcase theme, or By the sun turned on), a room gone to from Rooms ▾ or from a room chip, and a room set placed in Furnish. Never which theme, room or set. Nothing is sent while the usage report is off.

title: The usage report can say where you heard about PadSpan; Doors and windows go with their room in Layout
body_markdown:
### New
- **One optional question after you opt in to the usage report: where did you hear about PadSpan?** When you turn the report on from the card, the same card asks it once, with one-tap answers (Reddit, YouTube, the Home Assistant forum, another forum, the Marketplace or HACS, GitHub, Discord, a web search, a friend, somewhere else) and a Skip button. It is not asked again. If your report is already on, nothing pops up: the same choice is under Settings → Tracking → Help improve PadSpan, where you can set, change or clear it. The answer goes with the report as one word (`heard_from`), it is your own answer and never worked out from anything, and the Preview shows it. The README's list of what the report sends has the new line.

### Changed
- **A room moved in Mapping → Layout takes its doors and windows with it.** Doors, windows and doorways drawn in Live Aboard used to stay where the old wall was when a room was moved, turned or reshaped in Layout, and stood there on their own. Now, when you press **Save corrections**, each one on that room's walls goes with it: same width, same heights and settings, same place along its wall (as far from the nearer corner as it was, never past a corner). One that can't follow stays where it is: its wall is gone or now too short, or it is in a wall the room shares with a room that didn't move the same way. The message after Save, and a line under the button, says how many moved and how many stayed, so you can check those in Live Aboard's **Edit**. Nothing new is stored in Live Aboard's file.

title: Live Aboard: going back by itself puts the bars aside; Licence and update checks: simpler
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **When nobody has touched it for a while, Live Aboard goes back home with the bars aside**, the map alone, as it opens. Before, it brought the bars back. Your walls, Look and floors pulled apart stay as you left them; ☰ brings the bars back. Home view in Views ▾ still brings them back, as it's pressed by hand.
- **Each licence check is one request again.** 0.38.259 sent a hash of Home Assistant's instance ID and, while the licence server didn't read it, asked a second time with the ID. Now the ID goes once, in the body of the request with the key (never in the web address). The licence server keeps only a hash of it, as before.
- **The update and licence checks run once a day.** 0.38.259 added a timer that looked every hour whether a day had passed. The first check after Home Assistant starts still waits a random while, and a restart doesn't check again within 20 hours.
